newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close steady, seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close steady, seen easing.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Monday on new arrivals from the 1997/98 (July-June) crop and dealers said rates were likely to ease.
Dealer Oveis Razzak said the new crop was of good quality. Prices had risen in the past few days due to a shortage of funds, he added.

In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,300/2,325 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), K-68 at 2,525/2,550 and MNH-93 at 2,525/2,550. The new crop NIAB-78 was being sold at a slight premium over the old crop.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 109,694 375-lb bales of cotton by June 19 compared to 1.82 million at the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 144,965 bales by June 25 compared to 2.32 million a year ago.
